subject: using AIC and LogL to access need for geographic stratification

messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: using AIC and LogL to access need for geographic stratification
parts:
I am trying to access the need for geographic stratification in estimatin=
g=20
the detection function for a line transect survey of dolphins in a shallo=
w=20
lagoon system in Florida. The data has been pooled across surveys=20
(temporal replicates) to achieve necessary sample size, but there is no=20=

good ecological reason to suspect heterogeneity in detection function=20
between surveys. The total number of lines was 2697 and total line lengt=
h=20
is 8,611 km, with 818 sightings. I have settled on using the ungrouped=20=

distance data with truncation at 400m. There are 4 geographic strata=20
which are different water bodies. We believe that detection functions ma=
y=20
have differed between geographic strata due to differences in water depth=
,=20
clarity and wave activity. The final abundance estimates will be=20
estimated by temporal periods (8) and geographic strata (4).=20

When I fit the model with 4 geographic strata, AIC =3D 9231.2 (k=3D9, Log=
L=3D -
4606.60) and without strata AIC =3D 9226.44 (k=3D5, LogL=3D -4608.22). C=
learly,=20
the model without strata is better supported. The problem is when I look=
=20
at the fit of the detection function with no strata, it is terrible. By=20=

contrast, the fit of the detection functions among the geographic strata=20=

were all adequate. At this point, I=92m more comfortable with using the=20=

geographic stratification, but I=92m wondering if I=92m missing something=
more=20
fundamental. I can see why the model with strata is penalized for extra=20=

parameters (k=3D9 versus k=3D5). But why does the likelihood go down for=
the=20
no strata model, if the model does not fit as well as the individual=20
strata models do?
